exercises.q: Зелёный абажур рассеивает по ___ (комната) тёплый свет.
exercises.prompt: The green lampshade casts a warm glow in the room.
exercises.why: Они едут по дороге.* **По** may mean "about", "around": *Он ходит по комнате. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 28. exercises.q: Благодаря ___ (чуда) современной ветеринарии наши питомцы живут намного дольше.
exercises.prompt: Thanks to the marvels of modern veterinary medicine, our pets are living much longer lives.
exercises.why: Она дала деньги музею Судно шлo по морю Саша идёт к школе Борис побеждал благодаря его друзьям* Adjectives modifying masculine or neuter nouns in the dative case have the ending **-ому**. If they end in the 5-letter rule (**ш, щ, ч, ж**, or **ц**) or have the soft ending (-**ний**), their dative ending is **-ему**. Feminine adjectives have **-ой** or, after the 5-letter rule or soft ending, **-ей**. Essentially, these are the same as e prepositional endings, with masculine and neuter adjectives having an extra **-у** - the same ending most masculine and neuter nouns get.* — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  «The preposition к (to, towards, in the direction of …) always requires the dative case … The preposition по means "along" and is used with the dative case.» — DLI, Lessons 28–29.
exercises.context: Она дала деньги музею Судно шлo по морю Саша идёт к школе Борис побеждал благодаря его друзьям

exercises.q: Согласно ___ (иные источники), Ноам Чомски — самый цитируемый из ныне живущих авторов.
exercises.prompt: According to some sources, Noam Chomsky is the most cited living author.
exercises.why: Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending **-ой** if stressed: **новый** — **молодой**; **русский** — **плохой**, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension. — DLI, Lessons 46 and 47.  ·  «The preposition к (to, towards, in the direction of …) always requires the dative case … The preposition по means "along" and is used with the dative case.» — DLI, Lessons 28–29.
exercises.context: Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending **-ой** if stressed: **новый** — **молодой**; **русский** — **плохой**, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.

exercises.q: Самураи жили по ___ (кодекс) чести - бусидо.
exercises.prompt: Samurai lived by a code of honor called "Bushido".
exercises.why: The preposition **по** means "along" and is used with the dative case: *Я иду по коридору. Они едут по дороге.* **По** may mean "about", "around": *Он ходит по комнате. Они ездят по городу.* Notice also: **по почте** — by mail; **по телефону** — by phone; **по радио** — by radio; **по делу** — on business. **Motion on/along/across a surface** - the most common meaning is movement across (e.g., crossing the road), or along (e.g., walking along the street), or about (i.e., moving all around the entirety of a surface), or otherwise moving in some fashion on top of some surface. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 28. From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  «The preposition к (to, towards, in the direction of …) always requires the dative case … The preposition по means "along" and is used with the dative case.» — DLI, Lessons 28–29.
exercises.context: The preposition **по** means "along" and is used with the dative case: *Я иду по коридору.

exercises.q: Вопреки ___ (слова) Билибина, известие, привезенное им, было принято радостно.
exercises.why: After the verb **давать-дать** the object given is in the accusative case; the person to whom the object is given is in the dative case: *Он даст словарь сыну.* After **посылать-послать** the object sent is in the accusative case; the person to whom the object is sent is in the dative case: *Я пошлю книгу брату.* After **говорить-сказать** the person to whom something is said is in the dative case: *Я скажу ему, что вы уже здесь.* — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0). From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lessons 28, 39.  ·  «The preposition к (to, towards, in the direction of …) always requires the dative case … The preposition по means "along" and is used with the dative case.» — DLI, Lessons 28–29.
exercises.context: After the verb **давать-дать** the object given is in the accusative case; the person to whom the object is given is in the dative case: *Он даст словарь сыну.* After **посылать-послать** the object sent is in the accusative case;…
